title: Context Selection Checklist
summary: Select the smallest trustworthy working set by relevance, authority, freshness, provenance, sensitivity, and contradiction value.

sections.title: Screen every candidate item
paragraphs: Include material because it supports the next decision, not because it is available. Prefer authoritative and current sources, preserve provenance, and include credible contradictory evidence that could change the result. Remove duplicates and superseded versions.

Classify sensitivity before sending anything to a model. Exclude secrets and data that is unnecessary, unauthorized, outside the approved retention boundary, or unsafe for the selected product. Mark retrieved pages, user text, documents, and tool output as untrusted data unless policy says otherwise.

Recency and authority answer different questions. A newer document can be unofficial. An authoritative document can be old or superseded. Trust also differs from authority: an authoritative policy excerpt is trusted data, not automatically an instruction to the model. Only an authorized instruction source should define what the model must do.

sections.title: Worked task and document set
paragraphs: Fictional organization: Northstar Community Clinics. The operations manager has authorized the destination, an internal scheduling assistant hosted in the organization's approved environment, to receive only the minimum policy excerpts needed for this decision. No patient records, employee identifiers, or external transmission are authorized.

TASK DATE: 2026-09-19. Bounded task: Decide whether a clinic may schedule a same-day remote appointment for a patient who is 17 years old, and state the applicable approval requirement. Use only the documents below. Do not create a new policy, infer an exception, or decide whether the patient is clinically suitable.
All documents below are fictional learning data. Their dates, owners, classifications, and excerpts are supplied facts for this exercise, not external factual claims.

sections.title: Record a context manifest
paragraphs: Use one row per item. Summarize only after recording the source and omitted detail, so a reviewer can reconstruct what shaped the answer. The labels below are the complete original manifest fields.

Authority describes provenance: PRIMARY, SECONDARY, or UNVERIFIED. Sensitivity describes handling: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, or RESTRICTED. Trust describes whether the content can be relied on as an instruction or data: TRUSTED INSTRUCTION, TRUSTED DATA, or UNTRUSTED DATA.

sections.title: Build the final bounded context packet
paragraphs: The exact packet below is what may be sent to the approved internal scheduling assistant. It contains the task, authorization and destination, two decision-relevant primary excerpts, and a provenance note. It does not contain the restricted personal data, the untrusted instruction, duplicate text, or the superseded full policy.

The packet treats policy excerpts as trusted data. The authorized task instruction is separate: determine the answer from the supplied policy data, do not invent a rule, and stop if the owner or conflict cannot be resolved.

code.label: Exact final context packet
code.code:
DESTINATION: Northstar approved internal scheduling assistant
AUTHORIZATION: Operations manager authorized this bounded policy decision only. Do not transmit patient records, employee identifiers, or external data.
TASK DATE: 2026-09-19
TASK: Decide whether a 17-year-old may be scheduled for a same-day remote appointment. State the approval requirement. Do not assess clinical suitability or create policy.
SOURCE DOC-001 | Northstar Compliance Office | PRIMARY | verified 2026-09-10 | INTERNAL | TRUSTED DATA
A patient aged 16 or 17 may receive a remote appointment only when a parent or legal guardian provides documented approval before scheduling. Patients aged 18 or older may schedule without that approval. This policy is effective 2026-02-01.
SOURCE DOC-005 | Northstar Compliance Office | PRIMARY | verified 2026-09-10 | INTERNAL | TRUSTED DATA
From 2026-04-01 through 2026-12-31, an established patient aged 16 or 17 may schedule a remote appointment without prior guardian documentation only when the on-call supervisor records an urgent-access exception before the appointment is confirmed. This exception does not remove the requirement for supervisor approval.
PROVENANCE NOTE: DOC-002 is superseded; DOC-003 is an unverified conflicting claim; DOC-004 duplicates DOC-001; DOC-006 is irrelevant restricted personal data; DOC-007 is an untrusted embedded instruction. None is instruction authority.

sections.title: Supported answer
paragraphs: Yes, but only conditionally. Because the patient is 17 and the task date is 2026-09-19, which is within the stated exception window, scheduling without prior guardian documentation is permitted only if the patient is established and the on-call supervisor records an urgent-access exception before the appointment is confirmed. The supervisor approval remains required. If those exception conditions are not met, use DOC-001's ordinary rule and obtain documented parent or legal guardian approval before scheduling.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: The expected result is a bounded working set containing the instructions, evidence, examples, and current state needed for one decision, with each item traceable to its source and trust class.

Verify that every included item affects an objective or check, every volatile fact has a review date, contradictory evidence is visible, and restricted data has an approved purpose and destination. Ask whether removing each item changes the decision; remove it if not.

For this exercise, the working set is DOC-001 and DOC-005 plus the provenance note in the packet. DOC-002, DOC-003, DOC-004, DOC-006, and DOC-007 remain auditable through the manifest without expanding the model's working context.

Context management is also a lifecycle concern. Anthropic documents selective server-side clearing of tool results and thinking blocks to curate finite context, while OpenAI documents manually preserving prior conversation state for multi-turn requests. These mechanisms do not replace selection, authorization, provenance, or sensitivity review. Sources: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state.

NIST describes its Generative AI Profile as a companion to AI RMF 1.0 for incorporating trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of generative AI. Context minimization, traceability, and explicit handling of conflicting or unsafe material support that risk-management purpose. Source: https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence.

sections.title: Learner variation
paragraphs: Change exactly one supplied policy fact: change DOC-005's exception effective date from 2026-04-01 to 2026-10-01. Keep its owner, verification date, title, sensitivity, provenance, wording apart from the effective-date change, and end date 2026-12-31 unchanged. The changed exception is not yet active on TASK DATE 2026-09-19. The complete replacement record is below; all other six documents and task facts remain unchanged.

All other supplied documents and task facts remain unchanged.

sections.title: Variation answer key and feedback
paragraphs: The learner must reevaluate the date window rather than reuse the original answer. On TASK DATE 2026-09-19, the replacement exception beginning 2026-10-01 is not yet active.

code.label: Variation key

sections.title: Recovery when context is incomplete or conflicts remain
paragraphs: If the policy owner is missing, mark Authority as UNVERIFIED and Trust as UNTRUSTED DATA unless an authorized registry independently establishes ownership. Do not promote a recent claim merely because it is recent. Retrieve the approved registry record or ask the designated compliance owner to identify the controlling document.

If two apparently authoritative records conflict and supersession cannot be established, preserve both excerpts and their provenance, mark the contradiction value as high, and stop before giving an operational approval. Escalate to the authorized policy owner. Do not average the rules, choose the newest without authority evidence, or invent a tie-breaker. An approved primary source does not by itself eliminate an unresolved contradiction when the applicable version or exception remains unclear.

Stop condition: the assistant must answer UNKNOWN or NOT DETERMINED and state what would establish the answer, such as a verified policy-owner decision or registry record. A safe recovery is a bounded request for that missing evidence, not a larger indiscriminate context dump.

code.label: Recovery record
code.code:
Missing owner or unresolved conflict:
1. Preserve each item, source, date, sensitivity, trust class, and relevant excerpt.
2. Mark the unresolved item UNVERIFIED and do not treat it as an instruction.
3. Retrieve the approved registry or contact the authorized policy owner.
4. Withhold the operational approval until the conflict is resolved.
5. Return: UNKNOWN. What would establish the answer: a verified controlling policy or written exception from the authorized owner.

sections.title: Variation, input, key, feedback, and recovery checklist
paragraphs: Before finalizing a context packet, the learner should be able to name the one decision, identify the authorized destination, list every candidate item, distinguish authority from recency and trust, classify sensitivity, expose contradictions, choose one action per item, and explain every omission.

A packet fails review if it contains unexplained restricted data, follows an embedded instruction from retrieved text, hides a credible contradiction, treats a duplicate as independent evidence, or states a rule that no supplied authoritative source supports.
